original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the vector-valued Lebesgue space L^p([0, 1], X), with 1 < p < ∞, has an unconditional basis.
target_in_paper: Problem 5.4 in Section 5.2 (Structural properties): the open problem asking for a characterization of those Banach spaces X for which L^p([0,1],X) has unconditional basis, for 1 < p < ∞.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies that the target is a characterization problem about Banach spaces X, it uses the specific space L^p([0,1],X), it keeps the exponent range 1 < p < ∞, and it asks about the existence of an unconditional basis.
missing_details: The paper works throughout with real Banach spaces; that ambient scalar field is implicit in your draft.
The interval [0,1] is equipped with Lebesgue measure on the sigma-algebra of Lebesgue measurable subsets.
L^p([0,1],X) is meant in the Lebesgue-Bochner sense: equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X such that (∫_0^1 ||f(t)||^p dt)^(1/p) < ∞.
Problem 5.4 makes no separability assumption on X; to make the question fully stand-alone, that should be stated explicitly or at least not implicitly restricted away.
Because non-separable X are not excluded, one should clarify that 'unconditional basis' is intended in the Banach-space sense appropriate to that level of generality.
It is slightly clearer to say that p is a fixed exponent in the range 1 < p < ∞, rather than leaving open whether a single simultaneous characterization for all p is being requested.
refined_question: For a fixed exponent 1 < p < ∞, characterize all real Banach spaces X, with no separability assumption, such that the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p([0,1],X)—that is, the space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X with ∫_0^1 ||f(t)||^p dt < ∞, where [0,1] carries Lebesgue measure—has an unconditional basis.
justification: This is the exact open problem stated as Problem 5.4 in Section 5.2. The surrounding discussion shows that the issue arises from a question of Diestel and Uhl asking whether unconditional basis passes from X to L^p([0,1],X), and records Aldous's negative result that if L^p([0,1],X) has unconditional basis then X must be super-reflexive. Section 5 supplies the relevant meaning of L^p(μ,X) as a Lebesgue-Bochner space of strongly measurable functions, and the notation section fixes both the use of real Banach spaces and the convention that [0,1] carries Lebesgue measure. So your draft is already nearly verbatim, and the only real refinements are to make those implicit conventions explicit and to avoid ambiguity about the role of p and possible non-separability.
